wallet_storage.observation: BrowserCoin v1 persists privateKeyHex in localStorage and exports privateKeyHex in wallet JSON.
wallet_storage.inference_boundary: This is an implementation observation, not by itself a claim that a compromise occurred.

bootstrap.observation: BrowserCoin node startup uses P2P plus helper/bootstrap-server synchronization paths.
bootstrap.inference_boundary: Use only as an assurance prompt; architectural difference is not a FAE defect.

principles: Competitor has weakness != FAE needs new subsystem.
Does the observed weakness expose an untested or insufficiently evidenced FAE premise?

challenges.browsercoin_observation: 150 s target, 50 BRC initial subsidy and 210,000-block halving make issuance eras roughly one year; this motivates checking whether issuance outruns participation formation.
challenges.premise: Issuance cadence and monetary timing must be evaluated with participation/decentralization evidence rather than copied from another network.
challenges.unproven_remainder: No empirical result proves a universally sufficient wall-clock distribution for broad participation.
challenges.actual_gap: No BrowserCoin-derived ownership gap. The question is already inside the economic research owner.
challenges.required_action: Do not create a new frontier and do not change active economics. Continue only the existing economic evidence path under separate authority.
challenges.residual_uncertainty: Social participation/distribution adequacy remains empirical and research-bound.

challenges.browsercoin_observation: Sandglass v3 uses a 512 KiB scratch space, four dependent chains and serial dependent accesses; intra-hash dependency does not bound many-hash FPGA/ASIC parallelism.
challenges.existing_fae_owner: ASIC Lab / DP6 Robust Premise Review
challenges.premise: A competent specialized DP6 implementation must be bounded against the commodity-participation property using technology-calibrated PPA/economic evidence.
challenges.unproven_remainder: Full frozen-DP6 named-library standard-cell PPA, RW5 ASIC PPA, memory-interface/package coefficients and specialist LCVW remain incomplete.
challenges.actual_gap: The specialized bound remains unproven, but it is already explicitly owned and gated; BrowserCoin reveals no second ASIC frontier.
challenges.required_action: Continue only RP-B3-T1 when its non-production tool/library evidence gate is available; keep ASIC Lab HOLD otherwise.
challenges.target_frontier: RP-B3-T1 — Frozen-DP6 Named-Library Standard-Cell PPA Calibration
challenges.authority_impact: No DP6/consensus change and no AWS/FPGA/AFI/F2/paid-provider run authorized.

challenges.browsercoin_observation: Foreground benchmark competitiveness does not establish browser lifecycle, background scheduling, thermal, screen-state or normal-use parity.
challenges.existing_fae_owner: Representative Device Evidence + Representative Device Physical Autopilot
challenges.premise: Representative devices must sustain FAE mining under normal use and lifecycle transitions with provenance-bound physical evidence.
challenges.unproven_remainder: The frozen four-class PHYSICAL_EVIDENCE portfolio has not yet been completed.
challenges.actual_gap: No design-assurance ownership gap. The existing contract already requires sustained mining, normal-use coexistence, lifecycle recovery, thermal/energy evidence and recovery bounds.
challenges.required_action: Continue the existing physical frontier only when real selected devices execute the frozen protocol.
challenges.authority_impact: No synthetic physical PASS and no provider spending authorized.
challenges.residual_uncertainty: Real device-class results remain an external physical-evidence gate.

challenges.browsercoin_observation: A browser wallet must treat delivered code/origin and signing substitution as distinct from cryptographic key-at-rest protection.
challenges.existing_fae_owner: Persistent Vault / Wallet Onboarding + Public Code Security + Release Provenance
challenges.premise: For an honest runtime executing the exact admitted release artifact, the user-reviewed send intent must equal the payload actually signed and the delivered artifact must be provenance-bound.
challenges.unproven_remainder: The dedicated intent-freeze/substitution regression and exact reviewed-intent-to-signing-payload gate remain to be implemented and independently verified; arbitrary malicious same-origin JavaScript remains explicitly outside the claim.
challenges.actual_gap: A narrow assurance gap exists between current direct DOM intent capture and the exact payload signed; at-rest vault hardening alone does not close it.
challenges.required_action: Keep the acceptance contract/probe; serialize any signing-path implementation with the active Persistent Vault owner instead of creating a second wallet implementation.
challenges.target_frontier: Wallet Persistent Vault / Public Code Security signing-integrity hardening
challenges.authority_impact: No wallet key/spend authority, release or deployment authority consumed.
challenges.residual_uncertainty: Implementation is blocked by shared-state serialization, not by lack of a defined assurance requirement.

challenges.browsercoin_observation: Browser-first nodes need evidence that bootstrap, reconstruction and validation remain viable as chain age and stored history grow; current-age success alone is insufficient.
challenges.existing_fae_owner: Independent Node + Full-target Headers Sync + Mainnet Readiness
challenges.premise: A fresh or recovering independently operated node must reconstruct and validate canonical state as history grows without trusting an official snapshot or silently crossing an implementation ceiling.
challenges.unproven_remainder: Authoritative peer sync has MAX_BRANCH_BLOCKS=50,000 and fails closed above that branch length; no authoritative long-horizon scale/pruning/archival closure is proven.
challenges.actual_gap: A real scale ceiling is now explicit. The correct next question is evidence for a bounded scaling strategy, not immediate removal of the safety ceiling.
challenges.required_action: Research/measure long-horizon scale and recovery inside the existing node owner before selecting iterative sync, persistence, pruning/archival or another implementation.
challenges.authority_impact: No consensus-observable pruning/archival semantics or activation change authorized.
challenges.residual_uncertainty: The correct safe architecture beyond 50,000 blocks is not yet evidence-selected.

challenges.browsercoin_observation: Decentralized block production does not itself prove that a fresh node can discover and validate the network when official bootstrap infrastructure is absent.
challenges.existing_fae_owner: Peer Isolation/Eclipse + Independent Node + Mainnet Readiness
challenges.premise: A fresh device must have an explicitly specified independently controlled bootstrap path; mathematical zero-seed discovery is not required, but official-infrastructure dependence must not be hidden.
challenges.unproven_remainder: Production bootstrap roots remain intentionally unset and no independently administered real-WAN official-infrastructure=0 rehearsal is admitted.
challenges.actual_gap: The zero-seed negative control is proven; independent bootstrap topology plus real-WAN proof remain unproven.
challenges.required_action: Specify an independently administered bootstrap topology under the existing owner, then obtain external real-WAN evidence; do not invent a new discovery subsystem.
challenges.target_frontier: Peer Isolation/Eclipse + Independent Node cold-start evidence
challenges.authority_impact: No production bootstrap selection, paid provider execution or deployment authorized.
challenges.residual_uncertainty: Real-world administrator/failure-domain independence remains external evidence.

challenges.browsercoin_observation: Height/time-gated forks and release mechanics do not alone answer who may authorize changes or how maintainer disagreement/emergency changes are handled.
challenges.existing_fae_owner: Mainnet Readiness + Activation Boundary + Release Provenance/Independent Verifier
challenges.premise: Consensus changes must have explicit authority, deterministic activation compatibility, fail-closed version/policy mismatch handling and survivable procedures for disagreement/emergency cases.
challenges.unproven_remainder: The review did not locate authoritative evidence defining maintainer-disagreement and emergency-change procedure. Missing search evidence is not proof that no such architecture exists.
challenges.actual_gap: Evidence/documentation gap only at present; a new governance subsystem is not justified.
challenges.required_action: Perform bounded evidence reconstruction inside Mainnet Readiness before considering any governance hardening.
challenges.authority_impact: No consensus, activation-height, release or governance authority change authorized.
challenges.residual_uncertainty: Social/process survivability remains less evidenced than technical activation/release boundaries.

verification.provider_status_note: Vercel status contexts are outside this bounded review and were observed separately as build-rate-limit failures; no paid-provider action is authorized or required for this assurance result.

cii.reason: No challenge justified new architecture/systemic ownership. Three gaps are bounded hardenings of existing owners; governance is research-only; three challenges require no new action from this review.
